source_blocks.html:
Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
These tools can help you win every argument—not in the unhelpful sense of beating your opponents but in the better sense of learning about the issues that divide people, learning why they disagree with us and learning to talk and work together with them. If we read others' arguments generously and well, we might still disagree with them, but we will at least understand them—and understanding them is a prerequisite for any productive subsequent action.
这些工具能帮你赢得每一场争论——不是以击败对手这种无益的方式，而是以更好的方式：了解使人们分裂的议题，了解他们为何与我们的意见相左，并学会与他们交谈、合作。如果我们宽厚而妥善地阅读他人的论点，或许仍会不同意他们，但至少能理解他们——而理解他们，是任何富有成效的后续行动的前提。
B
Of course, many discussions are not so successful. Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly. We should also learn to present our own arguments honestly, clearly, and gracefully.
当然，许多讨论并不如此成功。尽管如此，我们仍须谨慎，不要过快指责对方论据拙劣。我们也应当学会诚实、清晰而优雅地呈现自己的论点。
C
None of these will be easy but you can start even if others refuse to. Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and explicitly consider opposing positions and the strengths they may have. This can seem confrontational, but it's actually a well-established rhetorical technique: conceding the strengths of others' arguments.
这些都并不容易，但即使他人拒绝，你也可以开始。下次你陈述立场时，为你所主张的内容构建论证，并明确考虑对立立场及其可能的可取之处。这看似对抗，实则是一种公认的老练修辞技巧：承认他人论点的长处。
D
Carnegie would be right if arguments were fights, which is how we often think of them. Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied. Even when you win, you end up no better off than before the argument. Winning a fight does not win you friends.
若争论是打架——我们也常这样看待它——卡耐基就对了。如同肢体冲突，言语之战也会让双方都流血。即便你赢了，境况也不比争论前更好。打赢一架并不能为你赢得朋友。
E
In his 1936 work How to Win Friends and Influence People, Dale Carnegie wrote: "there is only one way…to get the best of an argument—and that is to avoid it." While that approach might silence or placate your opponent, it does nothing to change the fact that you may be wrong and the other person may be right.
戴尔·卡耐基在1936年的著作《如何赢得朋友和影响他人》中写道："只有一个办法……在争论中占上风——那就是避免争论。"尽管那种做法或许能让对手沉默或平息，却丝毫改变不了你可能错、而对方可能对的事实。
F
These views of arguments also undermine reason. If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don't get caught. You will be rewarded for crushing your opponent, not for finding the truth. This is a mistake.
这些对争论的看法也损害了理性。如果你把一场对话看作打架或竞赛，那么只要不被抓到，你尽可以靠欺骗取胜。你会因击垮对手而非发现真相而受奖赏。这是个错误。
G
There is a better way to win arguments. Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not. You present a number of cogent arguments. They are good, but you can do better. Instead of automatically criticizing my otherwise cogent arguments, you would show that my position is plausible, by revealing the contexts in which it is valid.

Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
These tools can help you win every argument—not in the unhelpful sense of beating your opponents but in the better sense of learning about the issues that divide people, learning why they disagree with us and learning to talk and work together with them. If we read others' arguments generously and well, we might still disagree with them, but we will at least understand them—and understanding them is a prerequisite for any productive subsequent action.
这些工具能帮你赢得每一场争论——不是以击败对手这种无益的方式，而是以更好的方式：了解使人们分裂的议题，了解他们为何与我们的意见相左，并学会与他们交谈、合作。如果我们宽厚而妥善地阅读他人的论点，或许仍会不同意他们，但至少能理解他们——而理解他们，是任何富有成效的后续行动的前提。
B
Of course, many discussions are not so successful. Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly. We should also learn to present our own arguments honestly, clearly, and gracefully.
当然，许多讨论并不如此成功。尽管如此，我们仍须谨慎，不要过快指责对方论据拙劣。我们也应当学会诚实、清晰而优雅地呈现自己的论点。
C
None of these will be easy but you can start even if others refuse to. Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and explicitly consider opposing positions and the strengths they may have. This can seem confrontational, but it's actually a well-established rhetorical technique: conceding the strengths of others' arguments.
这些都并不容易，但即使他人拒绝，你也可以开始。下次你陈述立场时，为你所主张的内容构建论证，并明确考虑对立立场及其可能的可取之处。这看似对抗，实则是一种公认的老练修辞技巧：承认他人论点的长处。
D
Carnegie would be right if arguments were fights, which is how we often think of them. Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied. Even when you win, you end up no better off than before the argument. Winning a fight does not win you friends.
若争论是打架——我们也常这样看待它——卡耐基就对了。如同肢体冲突，言语之战也会让双方都流血。即便你赢了，境况也不比争论前更好。打赢一架并不能为你赢得朋友。
E
In his 1936 work How to Win Friends and Influence People, Dale Carnegie wrote: "there is only one way…to get the best of an argument—and that is to avoid it." While that approach might silence or placate your opponent, it does nothing to change the fact that you may be wrong and the other person may be right.
戴尔·卡耐基在1936年的著作《如何赢得朋友和影响他人》中写道："只有一个办法……在争论中占上风——那就是避免争论。"尽管那种做法或许能让对手沉默或平息，却丝毫改变不了你可能错、而对方可能对的事实。
F
These views of arguments also undermine reason. If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don't get caught. You will be rewarded for crushing your opponent, not for finding the truth. This is a mistake.
这些对争论的看法也损害了理性。如果你把一场对话看作打架或竞赛，那么只要不被抓到，你尽可以靠欺骗取胜。你会因击垮对手而非发现真相而受奖赏。这是个错误。
G
There is a better way to win arguments. Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not. You present a number of cogent arguments. They are good, but you can do better. Instead of automatically criticizing my otherwise cogent arguments, you would show that my position is plausible, by revealing the contexts in which it is valid.
有一种更好的方式去赢得争论。想象你赞成提高本州的最低工资，而我不赞成。你提出若干有力的论点。它们不错，但你还能做得更好。你不会自动地批评我那些本也站得住脚的论点，而是会揭示其成立的语境，从而表明我的立场也有其合理之处。

source_blocks.html:
参考范文

As is vividly depicted in the cartoon, two climbers are struggling halfway up a mountain. One, exhausted, complains, "I'm tired. I quit," while the other urges him, "Don't give up! Just rest a while, then keep climbing."

The drawing conveys an inspiring message: on the road to any goal, fatigue is natural, but quitting is never the answer. A proper rest merely recharges us; what ultimately counts is the resolve to press on. This holds especially true for a student preparing for the graduate entrance exam. There will be days when weariness and self-doubt overwhelm us, yet those who pause to catch their breath and then continue are the ones who reach the summit. Giving up halfway would waste all the effort already invested.

From my perspective, perseverance is the single most decisive factor between success and failure. Instead of yielding to momentary tiredness, we should rest strategically and keep moving, for the peak belongs to those who never truly stop.

【译文】

如漫画生动描绘，两名登山者正在半山腰艰难前行。一人精疲力竭地抱怨："累了，我不爬了"；另一人则劝道："别放弃！歇一下，接着爬。"

这幅画传递了鼓舞人心的讯息：在通往任何目标的路上，疲惫是常态，但放弃绝不可取。适度的休息只是为我们充电；真正关键的是继续前行的决心。对备战考研的学生而言尤其如此。总有些日子，疲惫与自我怀疑会将我们淹没，然而那些稍作喘息便继续前行的人，才是登顶之人。半途而废只会让已付出的努力付诸东流。

在我看来，坚持是成败之间最具决定性的因素。与其向一时的疲惫屈服，不如策略性地休息、继续向前，因为山顶属于那些从未真正停下的人。

The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years, as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates. When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited to freshmen, to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses. College officials tend to emphasize that the goal of grade forgiveness is less about the grade itself and more about encouraging students to retake courses critical to their degree program and graduation without incurring a big penalty. That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges' own needs as well. For public institutions, state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention—so better grades can, by boosting figures like those, mean more money. And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students—who, at the end of the day, are paying the bill—feel they've gotten a better value for their tuition dollars, which is another big concern for colleges.

This year marks exactly two centuries since the publication of Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, by Mary Shelley. Even before the invention of the electric light bulb, the author produced a remarkable work of speculative fiction that would foreshadow many ethical questions to be raised by technologies yet to come.

今年恰逢玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦（又名现代普罗米修斯）》出版两百周年。甚至在电灯泡发明之前，这位作者就写出了一部非凡的科幻作品，它预示了未来技术将引发的诸多伦理问题。

Today the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) raises fundamental questions: "What is intelligence, identify, or consciousness? What makes humans humans?"

如今，人工智能（AI）的迅猛发展提出了根本性问题："什么是智能、身份或意识？是什么使人类成其为人类？"

What is being called artificial general intelligence, machines that would imitate the way humans think, continues to evade scientists. Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look, move, and respond like humans, similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as "Westworld" and "Humans."

所谓通用人工智能——即能模仿人类思维方式的机器——仍然让科学家捉摸不透。然而，人类依然着迷于那种外观、动作、反应都像人的机器人，就像最近热门科幻剧《西部世界》和《真实的人类》中描绘的那样。

Just how people think is still far too complex to be understood, let alone reproduced, says David Eagleman, a Stanford University neuroscientist. "We are just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine to get there."

斯坦福大学神经科学家大卫·伊格曼说，人类究竟如何思考，仍然太过复杂，难以理解，更别说复制了。"我们目前的处境是：还没有好的理论来解释意识究竟是什么，又该如何造出一台能拥有意识的机器。"

But that doesn't mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren't at hand. The coming use of autonomous vehicles, for example, poses thorny ethical questions. Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions. Their reactions may be a complex combination of instant reflexes, input from past driving experiences, and what their eyes and ears tell them in that moment. AI "vision" today is not nearly as sophisticated as that of humans. And to anticipate every imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem.

但这并不意味着涉及AI的关键伦理问题还遥不可及。例如，即将到来的自动驾驶汽车就提出了棘手的伦理问题。人类司机有时必须在瞬间做出决定。他们的反应可能是即时反射、过去驾驶经验的输入，以及那一刻眼睛耳朵所感的复杂结合。如今AI的"视觉"远不如人类精密。而要预见每一种可想象的驾驶情形，是个艰难的编程难题。

Whenever decisions are based on masses of data, "you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions," notes Tan Kiat How, chief executive of a Singapore-based agency that is helping the government develop a voluntary code for the ethical use of AI. Along with Singapore, other governments and mega-corporations are beginning to establish their own guidelines. Britain is setting up a data ethics center. India released its AI ethics strategy this spring.

一家总部位于新加坡、正协助政府制定AI伦理使用自愿准则的机构的首席执行官陈杰豪指出，只要决策基于海量数据，"你很快就会碰到一大堆伦理问题"。与新加坡一道，其他国家政府和大型企业也开始制定各自的指导方针。英国正在设立数据伦理中心。印度今年春天发布了AI伦理战略。

On June 7 Google pledged not to "design or deploy AI" that would cause "overall harm," or to develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms. It also pledged not to deploy AI whose use would violate international laws or human rights.

6月7日，谷歌承诺不会"设计或部署"会造成"全面伤害"的AI，不会开发AI制导武器，也不会将AI用于违反国际准则的监控。它还承诺不会部署使用起来会违反国际法或人权的AI。

While the statement is vague, it represents one starting point. So does the idea that decisions made by AI systems should be explainable, transparent, and fair.

尽管这份声明含糊，但它代表了一个起点。AI系统做出的决策应当可解释、透明、公平，这一理念同样如此。

To put it another way: How can we make sure that the thinking of intelligent machines reflects humanity's highest values? Only then will they be useful servants and not Frankenstein's out-of-control monster.

换句话说：我们如何能确保智能机器的思考反映人类最高尚的价值观？唯有如此，它们才会是有用的仆人，而不是弗兰肯斯坦那个失控的怪物。

paragraphs.html: The ruling is a victory for big chains with a presence in many states, since they usually collect sales tax on online purchases already. Amazon.com, with its network of warehouses, also collects sales tax in every state that charges it, though third-party sellers who use the site don't have to.

被推翻的案件规定：如果一家企业把顾客购买的商品寄到该企业没有实体存在（如仓库或办公室）的州，该企业就不必为该州代征销售税。如果没有被代收，顾客通常有责任自己向州政府缴纳销售税，但大多数人没意识到自己欠税，很少有人缴纳。

Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote that the previous decisions were flawed. "Each year the physical presence rule becomes further removed from economic reality and results in significant revenue losses to the States," he wrote in an opinion joined by four other justices. Kennedy wrote that the rule "limited States' ability to seek long-term prosperity and has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field."

Big chains have been collecting sales tax nationwide because they typically have physical stores in whatever state a purchase is being shipped to. 此前，许多只在一两个州有实体的卖家，在把商品寄到这些州以外地址时，一直得以避开征收销售税。使用eBay和Etsy（为小卖家提供平台）的卖家也一直未在全国代征销售税。根据周四的裁决，各州可通过法律，要求州外卖家向顾客代收本州销售税并上缴州政府。

The losers, said retail analyst Neil Saunders, are online-only retailers, especially smaller ones. Those retailers may face headaches complying with various state sales tax laws. The Small Business & Entrepreneurship Council advocacy group said in a statement, "Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs are not well served at all by this decision."

partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: These tools can help you win every argument—not in the unhelpful sense of beating your opponents but in the better sense of learning about the issues that divide people, learning why they disagree with us and learning to talk and work together with them. If we read others' arguments generously and well, we might still disagree with them, but we will at least understand them—and understanding them is a prerequisite for any productive subsequent action.
options.zh: 这些工具能帮你赢得每一场争论——不是以击败对手这种无益的方式，而是以更好的方式：了解使人们分裂的议题，了解他们为何与我们的意见相左，并学会与他们交谈、合作。如果我们宽厚而妥善地阅读他人的论点，或许仍会不同意他们，但至少能理解他们——而理解他们，是任何富有成效的后续行动的前提。

options.label: B
options.en: Of course, many discussions are not so successful. Still, we need to be careful not to accuse opponents of bad arguments too quickly. We should also learn to present our own arguments honestly, clearly, and gracefully.
options.zh: 当然，许多讨论并不如此成功。尽管如此，我们仍须谨慎，不要过快指责对方论据拙劣。我们也应当学会诚实、清晰而优雅地呈现自己的论点。

options.label: C
options.en: None of these will be easy but you can start even if others refuse to. Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and explicitly consider opposing positions and the strengths they may have. This can seem confrontational, but it's actually a well-established rhetorical technique: conceding the strengths of others' arguments.
options.zh: 这些都并不容易，但即使他人拒绝，你也可以开始。下次你陈述立场时，为你所主张的内容构建论证，并明确考虑对立立场及其可能的可取之处。这看似对抗，实则是一种公认的老练修辞技巧：承认他人论点的长处。

options.label: D
options.en: Carnegie would be right if arguments were fights, which is how we often think of them. Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied. Even when you win, you end up no better off than before the argument. Winning a fight does not win you friends.
options.zh: 若争论是打架——我们也常这样看待它——卡耐基就对了。如同肢体冲突，言语之战也会让双方都流血。即便你赢了，境况也不比争论前更好。打赢一架并不能为你赢得朋友。

options.label: E
options.en: In his 1936 work How to Win Friends and Influence People, Dale Carnegie wrote: "there is only one way…to get the best of an argument—and that is to avoid it." While that approach might silence or placate your opponent, it does nothing to change the fact that you may be wrong and the other person may be right.
options.zh: 戴尔·卡耐基在1936年的著作《如何赢得朋友和影响他人》中写道："只有一个办法……在争论中占上风——那就是避免争论。"尽管那种做法或许能让对手沉默或平息，却丝毫改变不了你可能错、而对方可能对的事实。

options.label: F
options.en: These views of arguments also undermine reason. If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don't get caught. You will be rewarded for crushing your opponent, not for finding the truth. This is a mistake.
options.zh: 这些对争论的看法也损害了理性。如果你把一场对话看作打架或竞赛，那么只要不被抓到，你尽可以靠欺骗取胜。你会因击垮对手而非发现真相而受奖赏。这是个错误。

options.label: G
options.en: There is a better way to win arguments. Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not. You present a number of cogent arguments. They are good, but you can do better. Instead of automatically criticizing my otherwise cogent arguments, you would show that my position is plausible, by revealing the contexts in which it is valid.
options.zh: 有一种更好的方式去赢得争论。想象你赞成提高本州的最低工资，而我不赞成。你提出若干有力的论点。它们不错，但你还能做得更好。你不会自动地批评我那些本也站得住脚的论点，而是会揭示其成立的语境，从而表明我的立场也有其合理之处。
